subject: Request: SOC 2 Type II & temporary attestation — portal access + scope clarification
messages:
From: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@healthcove.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Josh Patel <josh.patel@healthcove.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today — SOC 2 Type II and scope questions

Marissa / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team at HealthCove liked the routing and cost controls you showed. Two quick asks from our security review that came up during the call: 1) can you provide your latest SOC 2 Type II report (redacted is fine), and 2) do you have a bridge letter / temporary attestation we can present to our auditors while the report is in your portal?

Also: we need clarity on data residency and whether Redwood’s hosted product is acceptable for PHI under a BAA — we currently must show that processing will be limited to US regions and that log retention policy meets our 12‑month requirement. Could you confirm who on your side handles HIPAA/GDPR questions so we can loop them in?

Next steps from our side: if you can drop the report into a secure portal (link or credentials) and share a short note on the scope (what services/environments are included), we’ll start internal eval and follow up with any detailed evidence requests. Ideally we’d have something this week so our procurement cycle stays on track.

Thanks,
Amanda
Director, Information Security
HealthCove

--
Attachment: intake-notes.pdf (stub, 72 KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — SOC 2 Type II and scope questions

Amanda — great to hear the demo landed well. Ben and I will own the procurement flow; copying Rishi from our security team for HIPAA/GDPR specifics.

Quick recap / commitments:
- We can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and a temporary attestation / bridge letter.
- We will provision HealthCove a trust portal account with read-only access to the report and a small set of artifacts (attestation, system description, and control summaries).
- Rishi / security will confirm the exact environments covered (hosted API vs private deployments) and the log retention window.

Rishi — can you confirm if the hosted API (us-east-1) is within scope for the 2025 Type II report and whether we can provide a BAA statement for PHI processing? Also, I have a prospective timeline from HealthCove: they’d like access this week if possible.

Amanda — I’ll send a portal invite as soon as Rishi confirms scope. If you have a preferred contact for the vendor DDQ, send their name/email and we’ll route the questionnaire there.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: proposed-map-of-deliverables.txt (stub)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@healthcove.com>, Josh Patel <josh.patel@healthcove.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — SOC 2 Type II and scope questions

Marissa / Ben / Amanda,

Short answers up front: yes, we can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report (covering hosted API in us-east-1 for production traffic) and a temporary attestation / bridge letter. We can also sign a BAA for customers that require PHI protections; the hosted offering can be configured to restrict processing to US regions — we’ll include that in the portal notes.

What I need from HealthCove to scope any deeper evidence requests:
- Confirmation of expected data types (e.g., pseudonymized user data vs PHI)
- List of services/endpoints you expect to call (inbound API names or example routes)
- Whether you intend to ingest files (S3) or only text payloads

I’ve uploaded a redacted copy of our 2025 Type II report and a draft bridge letter to the trust portal and attached a short temporary‑attestation PDF to this thread for immediate use (redacted-soc2-typeii-2025.pdf, temporary-attestation-20260529.pdf). Bridge-letter-template.docx is also attached for your legal if they want to propose language.

Portal invite (one-time link) is below — it expires in 7 days. Please accept and let us know who should have read-only vs admin view.
https://trust.redwood.ai/portal/healthcove-invite?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...

Amanda, if you can respond with the three items above, we’ll prioritize any further artifact pulls. If HealthCove needs a faster turnaround on a specific control test, call out the control IDs and we’ll route to the engineering owner.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: redacted-soc2-typeii-2025.pdf (redacted; 1.8 MB), temporary-attestation-20260529.pdf (130 KB), bridge-letter-template.docx (48 KB)
From: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@healthcove.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Josh Patel <josh.patel@healthcove.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — SOC 2 Type II and scope questions

Thanks Rishi — I accepted the portal invite and downloaded the redacted report and attestation. That gets us 90% of the way there.

Quick answers:
1) Data types: we will be sending pseudonymized patient summaries (no raw PHI identifiers per our app flow) but we need BAA language in place before we begin sending any production samples.
2) Endpoints: we plan to use /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings initially. No file upload expected at launch.
3) Control focus: access control and log retention policies — our auditors will want specifics on how logs are stored and for how long.

Next step: Josh (cc’d) from procurement will share a small DDQ that maps to the controls we care about. If you can send the BAA and confirm the log retention timeframe (and whether audit logs include token-level trace for 12 months), we’ll move toward an LOA and procurement.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — this helps our timeline.

Amanda
Director, Information Security, HealthCove
